summary: Leave Policies: HR Admin configures accrual rates
description: HR Admin gets a Leave Policies page: each employee's accrual rate in days a month for each leave type that tracks a balance (Vacation, Sick), editable in place, with a record of every change. The PRD role list says the HR Admin configures leave policies and the BRD says policies are configured by HR, not self-service, but no user story or acceptance criterion describes a screen; until now the only way was SQL. Additive: no role or required-feature change (golden rule). The monthly accrual job and its idempotency are not changed: a new rate applies from the next accrual, a month already accrued is never rewritten, nothing is paid back. Only employees have a policy (EPIC-10). Decided with the user on 2026-10-20 as the replacement for EPIC-8 (user management with email invites), which is deferred.

New migration 20261020120000_leave_policy_changes.sql: one row per change (employee, leave type, who, old rate, new rate, when), the new rate bounded 0 to 31, old rate null for a first policy, a change must change the rate, append-only update, delete and truncate triggers, RLS on, indexes for the two reads. verify_schema.sql counts the new table and probes every rule; types.ts mirrors it.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The table exists with RLS on and the bounds, and CI db-verify passes with its probes. 2. A row cannot be updated, deleted or truncated. 3. A rate above 31, below 0 or equal to the old rate is refused. 4. The migration is forward-only and the seed is untouched.

summary: Policy reads and the set-rate route
description: src/lib/leave/policies.ts: getPolicyPage (employees only, Vacation and Sick, search, 25 a page, clamped), getRecentPolicyChanges (last 10) and setPolicyRate (lock, checks in SQL, the rate and its change row in one transaction, an unchanged rate writes nothing); PUT /api/leave-policies (withErrorHandling, zod, assertRole hr_admin, the actor is the session user). A documented exception to AGENTS.md rule 3: HR's scope is the company.
acceptance_criteria: 1. HR reads employees with their rates and only HR does (the SQL checks the role). 2. HR sets a rate and the change row (who, old, new) is written with it. 3. An employee, a manager or a visitor is refused and nothing changes. 4. A negative, over-31, three-decimal, Unpaid, manager, HR or unknown target is refused and nothing changes. 5. A new rate is used from the next accrual and an accrued month is never rewritten; accrual stays idempotent. 6. Two HR Admins changing one rate at once leave a consistent old and new chain.

summary: Leave Policies page and nav item
description: /policies (HR only): a name search, a row per employee with a rate field per leave type and a Save button, pages of 25, recent changes, a note that a new rate applies from the next accrual; a white Leave Policies nav item for HR only between Calendar and Audit History. Two statements per page load.
acceptance_criteria: 1. HR sees the list, searches and pages; an employee or a manager is sent to the dashboard. 2. Saving shows a role=status message, an invalid or refused rate a role=alert message, and recent changes show the change. 3. Labels name the person and the type, 44px targets, keyboard usable, no horizontal scroll at 375 and 320 px. 4. The query budget stays within the pool.

description: Gated real-database tests (including the real accrual and its idempotency), mutation proofs, a browser check as HR at 1440, 768, 375 and 320 px with employee and manager refused, an 800-employee load check, the full quality gate, a retro.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The AC of TASK-070 to 072 hold on a real engine. 2. The browser check passes at 1440, 375 and 320 px. 3. The 800-employee read finishes well inside the query deadline and the figures are recorded. 4. The quality gate passes.

summary: Leave Policies for many employees: table, filters, sort, in-cell editing
description: Phase 1 of the redesign (from the user's ChatGPT mockup): three company-wide tiles, a search and filter card (team, leave type, status, sort, rows per page, removable chips), a table from xl with a sticky header, sortable columns, the manager under the name, Vacation and Sick edited in place (Enter or leaving the field saves, Esc reverts, saving, saved and error states), last changed (date by who) and a status badge; stacked cards below xl; a numbered pager; Recent changes beside the list from 2xl. No migration. Phase 2 (not built): row selection and bulk edit with a preview, a batch id so bulk changes read as one line, and a History view.
acceptance_criteria: 1. HR can search, filter by team, leave type and status, sort by name, rate or last changed, and choose 25, 50 or 100 rows. 2. A rate edited in place saves with its change record, shows saved or the error, and the row does not move. 3. The list stays fast and usable with thousands of employees (read about 1 ms to a few ms, 3 statements a page). 4. Employees and managers are still refused. 5. Keyboard, labels naming the person and the type, 44px targets, no horizontal scroll at 375 and 320 px.
